facts.fact: The twelve-story building contains 22 apartments of various sizes and layouts.
facts.quote: The 12-story structure contains 22 apartments of various sizes and layouts.

facts.fact: The open ground floor was designed to frame views of the Serra do Curral mountain range, though later surrounding development obstructed the view.
facts.quote: The Niemeyer Building's open ground floor was originally designed to frame views of the Serra do Curral mountain range behind the square. However, surrounding development in subsequent decades obstructed this view.

facts.fact: The modernist design was controversial at the time, with some opposing private residences in the public square.
facts.quote: Niemeyer's modernist design was controversial at the time, with some opposing the construction of private residence in the public square.

facts.fact: It was one of the first examples of modernist architecture in Belo Horizonte, completed before the famous works of Brasília.
facts.quote: The Niemeyer Building was one of the first examples of modernist architecture in Belo Horizonte, completed before the famous works of Brasília.

facts.fact: The building is listed at the municipal, state, and federal levels.
facts.quote: The building itself is listed at the municipal, state, and federal levels.

facts.fact: The museum is in Yinzhou District, Ningbo, Zhejiang, China, and opened on December 5, 2008.
facts.quote: It is located in Yinzhou District and opened on December 5, 2008.

facts.fact: It focuses on the history and traditional customs of the Ningbo area.
facts.quote: The museum focuses on Ningbo area history and traditional customs.

facts.fact: Wang Shu, the first Chinese citizen to win the Pritzker Architecture Prize in 2012, designed it.
facts.quote: Ningbo Museum was designed by Wang Shu, the first Chinese citizen to win the Pritzker Architecture Prize in 2012.

facts.fact: The design is a conceptual combination of mountains, water and oceans.
facts.quote: The design is a conceptual combination of mountains, water and oceans.

facts.fact: The architect collected stones and bricks from demolished structures nearby and let builders arrange them into walls using the wapan technique.
facts.quote: After collecting stones and bricks from demolished structures in the surrounding area, the architect gave the builders some freedom in arranging these to create walls, using the wapan technique.

facts.fact: Other walls are decorated with cement-covered bamboo, and the material depended on the angle at which each wall protrudes.
facts.quote: Other walls are decorated with cement-covered bamboos. Material used on different walls was decided by the angle at which the wall protrudes.

facts.fact: The first three levels form a united square with the main entrances and offices, and galleries are on the upper levels.
facts.quote: The first three levels create a united square, housing the main entrances and administrative offices. Galleries are housed on the upper levels.

facts.fact: The upper levels fracture, like the nearby mountains, into five smaller sections of sharp geometric shapes.
facts.quote: These upper levels fracture, like the mountains near the site, breaking into five smaller sections of sharp geometric shapes.

facts.fact: It is reported to be the first museum built with a large number of used materials.
facts.quote: It is reported that Ningbo Museum was the first museum built with a large number of used materials.

facts.fact: It won the Lu Ban Prize in 2009, the top architecture prize in China.
facts.quote: Ningbo Museum won the Lu Ban Prize in 2009, the top architecture prize in China.

facts.fact: It stands in the centre of Ulm, Germany, on the Münsterplatz (Minster Square).
facts.quote: The Stadthaus Ulm is in the centre of Ulm (Germany), located on the Münsterplatz (Minster Square).

facts.fact: It is used mainly for exhibitions of photography and modern and contemporary art.
facts.quote: Primarily, the building is used to present exhibitions of photography and modern and contemporary art.

facts.fact: Richard Meier set out to complement and contrast the Gothic style of Ulmer Münster.
facts.quote: The US architect Richard Meier attempted to complement and contrast the Gothic style of Ulmer Münster (German: Ulmer Münster) when he created the Stadthaus.

facts.fact: Meier's design was chosen in 1986, but a 1987 referendum voted narrowly against it; the council overruled the vote and building began in 1991.
facts.quote: The elected council, the Stadtrat, decided to rule against the narrow vote and construction began in 1991.

facts.fact: An open staircase connects its four levels, with views of the interior and the exterior beyond.
facts.quote: The Stadthaus provides a total area of 3,600 m on four levels, connected by an open staircase, with views of the interior and the exterior beyond.

facts.fact: Spanish Rosa Dante granite clads the building and also paves the terraces and the square, relating the materials to the surroundings.
facts.quote: The materials used in the building relate to the immediate surroundings: Spanish Rosa Dante granite was used in the cladding of the building, the floor of the terraces, and the pavement of the square.

facts.fact: The roof incline reflects the architecture of the neighbouring buildings.
facts.quote: The incline of the roof reflects the architecture of the neighboring buildings.

facts.fact: In 2019 it was listed as a monument significant to national heritage.
facts.quote: However, the Stadthaus was finished in 1993, and in 2019 the building was listed as monument significant to national heritage: 'Kulturdenkmal von besonderer Bedeutung'.

facts.fact: It is a constituent college of the University of Cambridge, with a primary focus on science, engineering and technology.
facts.quote: Churchill College is a constituent college of the University of Cambridge in Cambridge, England. It has a primary focus on science, engineering and technology, but retains a strong interest in the arts and humanities.

facts.fact: The campus architects were chosen in a competition with 19 entrants, in which Winston Churchill sat among the judges.
facts.quote: Following an architectural competition in which 19 entrants competed, the firm of Richard Sheppard, Robson & Partners was selected from a shortlist of four, with Sir Winston Churchill himself among the panel of judges.

facts.fact: Sheppard's modernist scheme is marked by brown brick walls, pre-cast concrete lintels and teak-framed glazing.
facts.quote: Richard Sheppard's resolutely modernist scheme for the campus - the hallmarks of which are brown brick walls, pre-cast concrete lintels, and teak-framed glazing - is softened by the extensive landscaped grounds in which the buildings are situated.

facts.fact: Landscape architect Sheila Haywood drew up the landscape master plan for the grounds in 1959.
facts.quote: The landscape architect Sheila Haywood drew up the landscape master plan in 1959 for the grounds.

facts.fact: The completed campus had nine main residential courts and a central building holding the dining hall, buttery, combination rooms and offices.
facts.quote: Construction was completed in 1968 with nine main residential courts and a central building consisting of the dining hall, buttery, combination rooms and offices.

facts.fact: The chapel has been described as a modern interpretation of a Byzantine basilica, a Greek cross marked out in concrete beams and exposed brick.
facts.quote: Sheppard's design for the Chapel has been described as a modern interpretation of a Byzantine basilica, a Greek cross marked out in concrete beams and exposed brick.

facts.fact: Inside the chapel, an exposed concrete frame is filled with brick, and eight narrow slit windows hold abstract stained glass by John Piper.
facts.quote: The concrete frame is exposed, filled with brick. Eight narrow vertical slit windows contain stained glass designed by John Piper and manufactured by Patrick Reyntiens.

facts.fact: The central buildings and chapel were each granted Grade II listed status in recognition of their architectural significance.
facts.quote: On 30 March 1993, the college's central buildings and chapel were separately granted Grade II listed heritage status in recognition of their architectural significance.

facts.fact: It is a housing estate in Pimlico, London, built in phases to a plan by Darbourne & Darke.
facts.quote: Lillington Gardens is an estate in the Pimlico area of the City of Westminster, constructed in phases between 1961 and 1971 to a plan by Darbourne & Darke.

facts.fact: It was among the last high-density public housing schemes built in London in the postwar period.
facts.quote: The estate was among the last of the high-density public housing schemes built in London during the postwar period and is referred to as one of the most distinguished.

facts.fact: It reached high housing density in a medium-rise structure rather than a high-rise one.
facts.quote: Notably, seven years before the Ronan Point disaster ended the dominance of the tower block, Lillington Gardens looked ahead to a new standard that achieved high housing density within a medium-rise structure rather than a high-rise structure.

facts.fact: It emphasised individuality in the grouping of dwellings and gave private gardens at ground and roof levels.
facts.quote: It emphasised individuality in the grouping of dwellings and provided for private gardens at ground and roof levels.

facts.fact: The planted gardens of its wide roof streets blend sympathetically with the surrounding Victorian terraces.
facts.quote: The estate's high build quality, and particularly the planted gardens of its wide "roof streets", blend sympathetically with the surrounding Victorian terraces.

facts.fact: The site surrounds the Grade I listed Church of St James the Less, and the whole estate became a conservation area in 1990.
facts.quote: The site surrounds the Grade I listed Church of St James the Less, built in 1859–61.

facts.fact: Nikolaus Pevsner called it easily the most interesting recent housing in inner London in 1973.
facts.quote: The architectural historian Nikolaus Pevsner described it in 1973 as "easily the most interesting recent housing in inner London".

facts.fact: The embassy is the Netherlands' diplomatic mission in Berlin, designed by Rem Koolhaas of OMA and opened in 2004.
facts.quote: Designed by Rem Koolhaas of OMA, the building was opened in 2004.

facts.fact: It stands on Roland Ufer in Mitte, next to the new government district.
facts.quote: The Netherlands, having sold their former embassy site after the War, was free to choose a new location and preferred Roland Ufer in Mitte, the oldest Berlin settlement, next to the (new) government district of their main trade partner.

facts.fact: The brief combined conventional civil service security with Dutch openness in a solitary building.
facts.quote: A solitary building, integrating requirements of conventional civil service security with Dutch openness was needed.

facts.fact: OMA fulfilled the block's perimeter with a podium yet built a freestanding cube, a mix of obedience and disobedience.
facts.quote: The office in the end realized the building in a combination of obedience (fulfilling the block’s perimeter) and disobedience (building a solitary cube).

facts.fact: A continuous trajectory reaching all eight storeys shapes the building's internal communication.
facts.quote: As the diplomats used the hallway in the old embassy building a lot for informal meetings OMA gave them a building with an enormous hallway as centre:  a continuous trajectory reaching all eight stories of the embassy shapes the building’s internal communication.

facts.fact: The workspaces are the leftover areas after the trajectory was carved out of the cube, and lie along the facade.
facts.quote: The workspaces are the ‘leftover areas’ after the trajectory was ‘carved’ out of the cube and are situated along the facade.

facts.fact: A diagonal void through the building lets people see the TV Tower from the park.
facts.quote: part of it is a ‘diagonal void’ through the building that allows to see the TV Tower from the park.

facts.fact: The trajectory also works as a main air duct from which fresh air percolates to the offices and is drawn off via the double facade.
facts.quote: The (slightly over pressurized) trajectory works as a main airduct from which fresh air percolates to the offices to be drawn off via the double (plenum) facade.

facts.fact: The design won the Architekturpreis Berlin in 2003 and the Mies van der Rohe Award for European Architecture in 2005.
facts.quote: Koolhaas's design won the Architekturpreis Berlin in 2003 and the Mies van der Rohe Award for European Architecture in 2005.

facts.fact: It is a shopping complex in central Tokyo built in 2005 by Mori Building.
facts.quote: Omotesando Hills (表参道ヒルズ, Omotesandō hiruzu) is a shopping complex in central Tokyo built in 2005 in a series of urban developments by Mori Building.

facts.fact: It occupies a 250-meter stretch of Omotesandō in Aoyama and contains over 130 shops and 38 apartments.
facts.quote: It occupies a 250-meter stretch of Omotesandō, a shopping and (previously) residential road in Aoyama.

facts.fact: It replaced the Bauhaus-inspired Dōjunkai Aoyama Apartments, built in 1927 after the 1923 Kantō earthquake.
facts.quote: The building replaced the Bauhaus-inspired Dōjunkai Aoyama Apartments, which had been built in 1927 after the 1923 Kantō earthquake.

facts.fact: The demolition raised questions about Japan's interest in preserving historic buildings.
facts.quote: The demolition of the apartments again raised questions about Japan's interest in preserving historic buildings.

facts.fact: A small section of the old apartments is reconstructed in the south-east part of the new complex.
facts.quote: A small section of the old apartments is reconstructed in the south-east part of the new complex.

facts.fact: It is a historic, still-operating filling station in Skovshoved on the northern outskirts of Copenhagen.
facts.quote: The Skovshoved Petrol Station (Danish: Skovshoved Tankstation) is a historic, still-operating filling station in Skovshoved at the northern outskirts of Copenhagen, Denmark.

facts.fact: Arne Jacobsen designed it, and it first opened in 1936 as an example of the functionalist style of the time.
facts.quote: First opened in 1936, it was designed by Arne Jacobsen and is an example of the functionalist style typical of the time.

facts.fact: It was originally commissioned by Texaco and is now operated by Uno-X.
facts.quote: The filling station was originally commissioned by Texaco but is now operated by Uno-X.

facts.fact: A projecting oval canopy, nicknamed The Mushroom, dominates the exterior.
facts.quote: The exterior of the building is dominated by the projecting oval canopy, colloquially known as "The Mushroom" (Danish: Paddehatten).

facts.fact: The canopy gives shade and shelter to motorists and, lit from beneath, doubles as a sign at night.
facts.quote: It offers shade and shelter for filling motorists and, illuminated from beneath, also doubles as a sign at night.

facts.fact: It is Class A listed and was thoroughly restored in 2002.
facts.quote: It is Class A listed and was thoroughly restored in 2002.

facts.fact: The main building now houses an ice cream parlour unrelated to the petrol business.
facts.quote: While the pumps and the roof are still used as a petrol station, the main building now houses an ice cream parlor, with no relation to the petrol station business and its operations.

facts.fact: It is a single-storey house in Wimbledon, designed in 1967 by Richard Rogers and Su Rogers and built in 1968–70.
facts.quote: 22 Parkside (also known as the Rogers House or Wimbledon House) is a residential property in Wimbledon, London, designed in 1967 by British architect Richard Rogers and his then wife, Su Rogers, and built in 1968–70.

facts.fact: It was designed for Rogers' parents.
facts.quote: 22 Parkside on the A219 is a single-storey house designed in 1967 for Rogers' parents (Dr. William Nino and Dada Rogers) by Rogers and his then wife, Su.

facts.fact: It sits in a narrow plot of woodland opposite Wimbledon Common.
facts.quote: Set in a narrow plot of woodland just opposite Wimbledon Common, the house was built in 1968–70.

facts.fact: It is made from bright yellow-painted steel ribs with full-height glazing at each end.
facts.quote: The single-storey modernist house is made from bright yellow-painted steel ribs with full-height glazing at each end, and is separated into two parts.

facts.fact: One part is a flat and pottery studio for Rogers' mother, with the main house set in trees behind.
facts.quote: The first part is a flat and pottery studio for Rogers' mother, with the main house set in trees behind.

facts.fact: Two opposite sides have ceiling-to-wall glass with views onto the courtyard and landscaped gardens.
facts.quote: Two opposite sides of the house, north-east and south-west, have ceiling-to-wall glass with views onto the grounds, which consist of a courtyard and landscaped gardens.

facts.fact: Rogers said its prefabricated steel and glass modules inspired much of his later work, including the Centre Georges Pompidou and Lloyd's building.
facts.quote: Rogers said that the approach he used to design this early work, such as the use of prefabricated steel and glass modules, served as an inspiration for much of his future work, which includes the Centre Georges Pompidou, co-designed with Renzo Piano, and the Grade I listed Lloyd's building.

facts.fact: English Heritage called it an early, executed example of a High-Tech, steel-framed house in Britain.
facts.quote: Architecturally, they called it "an early, executed example of a High-Tech, steel-framed house in Britain" commenting on the significance of "prefabricated components" and "neoprene gaskets".

facts.fact: It became Grade II* listed on 22 February 2013 and was later donated to Harvard's design school, then the National Trust.
facts.quote: Since 22 February 2013, it has been a Grade II* listed building.

facts.fact: It is a public art school in Vienna, founded in 1688 as a private academy.
facts.quote: The Academy of Fine Arts Vienna (German: Akademie der bildenden Künste Wien) is a public art school in Vienna, Austria. Founded in 1688 as a private academy, it is now a public university with more than 1,500 students and six institutes.

facts.fact: Its main building on Schillerplatz near the Ringstraße was planned by Theophil Hansen and inaugurated in 1877.
facts.quote: Its main building on Vienna's Schillerplatz near the Ringstraße boulevard was planned by Theophil Hansen and inaugurated in 1877.

facts.fact: Hansen's building was constructed as part of the layout of the Ringstraße boulevard.
facts.quote: A new building was constructed according to plans designed by Theophil Hansen in the course of the layout of the Ringstraße boulevard.

facts.fact: Interior works, including ceiling frescos by Anselm Feuerbach, continued until 1892.
facts.quote: On 3 April 1877, the present-day building on Schillerplatz in the Innere Stadt district was inaugurated; the interior works, including ceiling frescos by Anselm Feuerbach, continued until completion in 1892.

facts.fact: The academy houses an art collection that includes Hieronymus Bosch's The Last Judgement triptych and is open to the public.
facts.quote: The academy houses an expansive art collection that includes The Last Judgement triptych by Hieronymus Bosch, and is open to the public.

facts.fact: It has had university status since 1998 but kept its original name.
facts.quote: The academy has had university status since 1998, but retained its original name.

facts.fact: It is an ensemble of apartment buildings in Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines, a ville nouvelle near Paris and Versailles, built in 1981.
facts.quote: The Arcades du Lac, built in 1981, is an ensemble of apartment buildings in the outer Paris ville nouvelle of Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines, France, near Versailles.

facts.fact: Ricardo Bofill Taller de Arquitectura designed this mixed suburban housing and HLM complex.
facts.quote: The mixed suburban housing and HLM complex was designed by Ricardo Bofill Taller de Arquitectura as the centerpiece of an urban composition, with the central portion "Le Viaduc" jutting into an artificial lake from the shore.

facts.fact: The central portion, Le Viaduc, juts into an artificial lake from the shore.
facts.quote: The mixed suburban housing and HLM complex was designed by Ricardo Bofill Taller de Arquitectura as the centerpiece of an urban composition, with the central portion "Le Viaduc" jutting into an artificial lake from the shore.

facts.fact: The design was inspired by the Pont d'Avignon, Château de Chenonceau and the Aqueduct of Segovia.
facts.quote: The design was inspired by the Pont d'Avignon, Château de Chenonceau and the Aqueduct of Segovia.

facts.fact: Charles Jencks described it as an adaptation of Versailles, a Versailles for the people, noting influences of Claude Nicolas Ledoux in the detailing of the elevations.
facts.quote: The entire project was described by architecture critic Charles Jencks as an adaptation of Versailles as a "Versailles for the people" while noting influences of Claude Nicolas Ledoux in the detailing of the elevations.

facts.fact: Bofill intended a contrast between the new housing of the 1970s and 1980s and the earlier Le Corbusier-inspired housing of the 1950s and 1960s.
facts.quote: Bofill's design intention was to offer a contrast between the new housing of the 1970s and 1980s and the earlier Le Corbusier-inspired housing projects of the 1950s and 1960s.

facts.fact: It is a house in Brno, designed by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe and Lilly Reich and built between 1928 and 1930 for Fritz and Greta Tugendhat.
facts.quote: and was designed by the German architects Ludwig Mies van der Rohe and Lilly Reich. It was built  between 1928 and 1930 for Fritz Tugendhat and his wife Greta, of the wealthy and influential Jewish Czech Tugendhat family.

facts.fact: It was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2001.
facts.quote: Famous for its revolutionary use of space and industrial building materials, the building was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2001.

facts.fact: The free-standing three-storey villa sits on a slope and faces south-west.
facts.quote: The free-standing three-story villa is on a slope and faces the south-west.

facts.fact: Mies used an iron framework that let him dispense with supporting walls and arrange the interior for a feeling of space and light.
facts.quote: Mies used a revolutionary iron framework, which enabled him to dispense with supporting walls and arrange the interior in order to achieve a feeling of space and light.

facts.fact: The main living area has a curtain wall of large windows framing a view of Špilberk Castle, and two windows can be lowered fully into the floor.
facts.quote: Accordingly, the main living area features a curtain wall divided into multiple large windows, framing a panoramic view of Špilberk Castle; remarkably, two of these windows can be completely lowered into the floor, much like in an automobile.

facts.fact: A dividing wall of brown-gold onyx from the Atlas Mountains in Morocco separates the main living area.
facts.quote: The main living area features a dividing wall of brown-gold onyx, which Mies sourced from the Atlas Mountains in Morocco.

facts.fact: Mies specified all the furnishings in collaboration with Lilly Reich, including the Tugendhat and Brno chairs.
facts.quote: Mies specified all the furnishings, in collaboration with interior designer Lilly Reich (two armchairs designed for the building, the Tugendhat chair and the Brno chair, are still in production).

facts.fact: The building has air conditioning, unusual for its time.
facts.quote: Unusually for the time, the building features air conditioning.

facts.fact: The family fled in 1938; the Gestapo confiscated the villa in 1939, and it has been open to the public as a museum since 1994.
facts.quote: Since 1994 the villa has been open to the public as a museum administered by the city of Brno.

facts.fact: It is a prefabricated iron building in Maputo, built in Belgium and reassembled there in 1892.
facts.quote: The Casa de Ferro (English: Iron House) is a historic prefabricated iron building located in Maputo, Mozambique. Originally built in Belgium, the structure was bought by the Portuguese colonial government and reassembled in 1892 in Maputo (at the time named Lourenço Marques).

facts.fact: It was made by Societé Anonyme des Forges d'Aiseau using the Danly system, developed by the Belgian engineer Joseph Danly.
facts.quote: The Casa de Ferro was constructed in Belgium, in the workshops of the Societé Anonyme des Forges d'Aiseau, using a newly patented, state-of-the-art construction system developed by the Belgian engineer Joseph Danly and known as the Danly system.

facts.fact: It was intended as the governor's residence but was never inhabited, instead housing various institutions.
facts.quote: However, the building was never inhabited and has instead served as the seat of a variety of local and national institutions throughout its existence.

facts.fact: Popular belief blames the heat of the iron, but research suggests the governor's preference for a more traditional building mattered more.
facts.quote: According to popular belief, the decision was motivated by the insufferable heat produced by the iron's prolonged exposure to the tropical sun. However, research has established that the climate was a minor, if not outright irrelevant, factor in the unexpected turn of events, with the Governor's preference for a more traditionally constructed building playing a much more substantial part.

facts.fact: Danly-system buildings have a wrought iron structure with cast iron connecting pieces and thin embossed iron cladding panels.
facts.quote: Buildings constructed according to the Danly system feature a wrought iron structure, with cast iron connecting pieces and thin, embossed iron cladding panels with convex geometrical designs which serve both decorative and structural functions.

facts.fact: Panels on both the inside and outside of the frame leave clear internal space and let air circulate inside the walls.
facts.quote: The iron panels are mounted both on the inside and on the outside of the frame, leaving a clear internal space and thus allowing air to circulate freely inside the walls; internal ventilation is further ensured by holes pierced on the interior panels close to the ceilings, as well as by the numerous windows in each room.

facts.fact: No foundations are needed, which made construction and the later relocation simple and fast.
facts.quote: No foundations are needed for houses built with the Danly system, as the lightweight structures are simply mounted on top of an iron frame laid upon the ground; this made the construction and the later relocation of the Casa de Ferro simple and fast processes.

facts.fact: Claims that Gustave Eiffel designed it are unfounded.
facts.quote: However, claims that the building was designed by Eiffel are unfounded.

facts.fact: It is eclectic in style, reminiscent of Victorian architecture, three stories tall with a cross gable roof.
facts.quote: Eclectic in style, the Casa de Ferro has a design reminiscent of Victorian architecture, blending with Maputo's other late nineteenth-century colonial buildings, which were largely influenced by South African architecture.

facts.fact: It is a town house in Brussels designed by Paul Cauchie and built in 1905 in Art Nouveau style.
facts.quote: It was designed by the architect, painter, and designer Paul Cauchie [fr], and built in 1905, in Art Nouveau style.

facts.fact: Its facade is remarkable for its allegorical sgraffito decoration.
facts.quote: Its façade is remarkable for its allegorical sgraffito decoration.

facts.fact: It stands at 5, rue des Francs in Etterbeek, next to the Parc du Cinquantenaire.
facts.quote: The house is located at 5, rue des Francs/Frankenstraat in the municipality of Etterbeek, next to the Parc du Cinquantenaire/Jubelpark.

facts.fact: Cauchie designed the front to advertise and sell their work: sgraffito for him and art teaching for his wife.
facts.quote: He designed the front of the house with the intention of advertising and selling their work: sgraffito for him and art teaching for her.

facts.fact: The words Par Nous — Pour Nous (By Us — For Us) are drawn at the centre of the facade.
facts.quote: At the very centre of the façade, Cauchie drew the words "Par Nous — Pour Nous" (English: By Us — For Us).

facts.fact: It is a good example of the Gesamtkunstwerk, or total work of art, principle in architecture.
facts.quote: The Cauchie House is a good example of the application of the principle of a unified work of art or Gesamtkunstwerk ("total work of art") in architecture.

facts.fact: It stands on a narrow plot about 6 metres wide.
facts.quote: They married in 1905 and decided to build a house on the 6-metre-wide (20 ft) plot of land Cauchie bought at 5, rue des Francs/Frankenstraat, next to the Parc du Cinquantenaire/Jubelpark in Brussels.

facts.fact: The college's main building on its current campus in southern Mexico City was designed by the Mexican architect Teodoro González de León.
facts.quote: In 1976, the university's campus was moved from the Colonia Roma (a historic neighborhood just west of the city's center) to its current location in the southern portion of the capital; the main building of the campus was designed by the Mexican architect Teodoro González de León.

facts.fact: The Daniel Cosío Villegas Library sits in the centre of the campus and takes up about 30% of the building real estate.
facts.quote: The Daniel Cosío Villegas Library is a public academic library situated in the center of El Colegio de México's campus, contains around 700,000 volumes, and comprises 30% of the total building real estate.

facts.fact: El Colegio de México is a higher education institute specialising in social sciences and humanities.
facts.quote: El Colegio de México, A.C. (commonly known as Colmex, English: The College of Mexico) is a Mexican institute of higher education, specializing in teaching and research in social sciences and humanities.

facts.fact: It is a craft school on the coast of Deer Isle, Maine, founded in 1950.
facts.quote: Haystack Mountain School of Crafts, commonly called "Haystack," is a craft school located at 89 Haystack School Drive on the coast of Deer Isle, Maine.

facts.fact: The campus and buildings were designed by architect Edward Larrabee Barnes.
facts.quote: The campus and buildings were designed by architect Edward Larrabee Barnes, and consists of 34 buildings clustered onto 8 acres (3.2 ha) of the more than 40-acre (16 ha) campus property, located on Stinson's Neck, an appendage extending southeast from the main part of the island of Deer Isle.

facts.fact: Barnes designed the buildings to fit their environment and give views of the land and seascape.
facts.quote: The buildings were designed by Barnes to fit well within their environment, and to provide views of the surrounding land- and seascape.

facts.fact: The campus moved to Deer Isle in 1961.
facts.quote: In 1961 the school was moved to its current campus on Deer Isle.

facts.fact: In 1994 it won the AIA Twenty-five Year Award, given to a structure whose construction and original intent have withstood the test of time.
facts.quote: In 1994, the school campus won the "Twenty-five Year Award" from the American Institute of Architects.  The award is given to a structure (or in this case, several structures) whose construction and original intent have withstood the test of time.

facts.fact: The campus was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2005.
facts.quote: The school was honored again in 2005 when the campus was added to the National Register of Historic Places.

facts.fact: It is a contemporary art museum in Kanazawa, Japan, designed by Kazuyo Sejima and Ryue Nishizawa of SANAA.
facts.quote: The museum was designed by Japanese architects Kazuyo Sejima and Ryue Nishizawa of the architectural office SANAA in 2004.
facts.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, Kanazawa

facts.fact: It stands in the centre of Kanazawa, near Kenroku-en garden.
facts.quote: The Museum is located in the center of Kanazawa, near Kenroku-en garden and the Ishikawa Prefectural Museum of Art.
facts.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, Kanazawa

facts.fact: The building is circular, and the shape aims to keep its volume low, soften the scale and allow access from many entrances.
facts.quote: This shape aims to keep the appearance of the overall building volume low, to mitigate the scale of the project and allows access from multiple points of entry.
facts.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, Kanazawa

facts.fact: Its transparency expresses the wish to avoid the museum being seen as a large, introverted mass.
facts.quote: The transparency of the building further manifests the wish to avoid the museum being perceived as a large, introverted mass.
facts.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, Kanazawa

facts.fact: Community spaces such as a library, lecture hall and children's workshop sit on the periphery, with museum spaces in the middle.
facts.quote: The building includes community gathering spaces, such as a library, lecture hall, and children’s workshop, located on the periphery, and museum spaces in the middle.
facts.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, Kanazawa

facts.fact: The galleries vary in proportion and light, from daylit rooms under glass ceilings to rooms with no natural light.
facts.quote: The galleries are of various proportions and light conditions – from bright daylight through glass ceilings to spaces with no natural light source, their height ranging from 4 to 12 metres.
facts.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, Kanazawa

facts.fact: Four fully glazed internal courtyards bring daylight to the centre of the building.
facts.quote: Four fully glazed internal courtyards, each unique in character, provide daylight to the center of the building and a fluent border between community spaces and museum spaces.
facts.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, Kanazawa

facts.fact: Curators vetoed the architects' idea of many windows between galleries because they wanted the galleries more autonomous.
facts.quote: In earlier designs, the architects had hoped to puncture the independent galleries with many windows, through which visitors would feel connected with other rooms; the curators, who wanted the separate galleries to be more autonomous, vetoed that suggestion.
facts.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, Kanazawa

facts.fact: It is a stepwell in the village of Abhaneri in the Indian state of Rajasthan.
facts.quote: Chand Baori is a stepwell situated in the village of Abhaneri in the Indian state of Rajasthan.

facts.fact: It is named after a local ruler of the Nikumbh dynasty called Raja Chanda.
facts.quote: It is named after a local ruler of the Nikumbh dynasty called Raja Chanda, and its construction is dated to the 8th–9th centuries.

facts.fact: It has been built in an upside-down pyramid style.
facts.quote: It has 3500 steps cascading 13 stories deep into a massive tank at the bottom and has been constructed in an upside-down pyramid style.

facts.fact: No inscription has been found about who built the stepwell or the neighbouring Harshat Mata Temple, so it is dated by stylistic similarity to other terraced temples.
facts.quote: However, no epigraphic evidence has been found regarding the construction of the Chand Baori or the adjoining Harshat Mata Temple.

facts.fact: The state of Rajasthan is very dry, and the design of the stepwell was intended to conserve as much water as possible.
facts.quote: The state of Rajasthan is extremely arid, and the design and final structure of Chand Baori were intended to conserve as much water as possible.

facts.fact: At the bottom of the well the air stays cooler than at the surface, and the stepwell was used as a community gathering place during intense heat.
facts.quote: At the bottom of the well, the air remains 5-6 °C  cooler than at the surface, and Chand Baori was used as a community gathering place for locals during periods of intense heat.

facts.fact: Stepwells like this served several purposes besides drawing water, including religious and ceremonial activities.
facts.quote: Many of these stepwells, including Chand Baori, served multiple purposes alongside drawing water and played a significant role in religious and ceremonial activities.

facts.fact: The classical Indian architecture texts call this stepwell design a vijay vapi.
facts.quote: The classical Indian texts on architecture (Vastu) like Aparajitapriccha or Vishvakarma's Vastushastra  call this design a vijay vapi.

facts.fact: It is the complex where the Malaysian Parliament assembles, in the Perdana Botanical Gardens in Kuala Lumpur.
facts.quote: The Malaysian Houses of Parliament (Malay: Bangunan Parlimen Malaysia), also known as the Parliament House, is a complex where the Malaysian Parliament assembles.

facts.fact: The project was the idea of Tunku Abdul Rahman, the first Malayan Prime Minister, who saw it as the permanent seat of Parliament.
facts.quote: The construction of the current Houses of Parliament building was the brainchild of Tunku Abdul Rahman, the first Malayan Prime Minister.

facts.fact: A British architect from the Public Works Department, William Ivor Shipley, was assigned to lead the project.
facts.quote: In March 1960, William Ivor Shipley, a British architect from the Public Works Department was assigned to lead the project.

facts.fact: Before designing it, Shipley toured parliament buildings in India and Pakistan, and said the building need not necessarily use Islamic styles.
facts.quote: He also disclosed that the new parliament building for Malaya may not necessarily feature Islamic styles, and he was given a free hand by the government to design the new building.

facts.fact: The tropical climate was given priority in the design, and pools and lawns were planned to make hanging gardens that use water to cool the building.
facts.quote: Malaya's tropical climate will also be given prioritised consideration when designing the new Parliament House, and the building will be air-conditioned.

facts.fact: The facade was planned as a two-layer grill, giving structural strength and cooling.
facts.quote: The building will be covered in grill-like facade in two layers, which would give structural strength as well well as cooling-off the building.

facts.fact: The complex has two parts: a main building with the two legislative chambers and a tall tower holding representatives' offices.
facts.quote: The main building hosts the Dewan Rakyat (House of Representatives) and the Dewan Negara (Senate) while representatives' offices are located in the tower.

facts.fact: Construction fell behind schedule because of late-arriving materials, and the building was officially opened on 2 November 1963.
facts.quote: On 2 November 1963, the new Parliament House was officiated by Tuanku Syed Putra Jamalullail, the third Yang di-Pertuan Agong.

facts.fact: It is an 18-storey mixed-use building in Brumunddal, Norway, completed in March 2019.
facts.quote: Mjøstårnet (Norwegian for the tower of Mjøsa) is an 18-storey mixed-use building in Brumunddal, Norway, completed in March 2019.

facts.fact: When completed it was officially the world's tallest wooden building, until it was surpassed in August 2022.
facts.quote: At the time of completion, it was officially the world's tallest wooden building, at 85.4 m (280 ft) tall, before being surpassed by Ascent MKE in August 2022.

facts.fact: It holds a hotel, apartments, offices, a restaurant and common areas, with a swimming pool in an adjacent extension also built in wood.
facts.quote: The building offers a hotel, apartments, offices, a restaurant and common areas, as well as a swimming pool in the adjacent first-floor extension.

facts.fact: Voll Arkitekter designed it for AB Invest, and Moelven Limtre installed the timber structures.
facts.quote: Mjøstårnet was designed by Norwegian studio Voll Arkitekter for AB Invest. Timber structures were installed by Norwegian firm Moelven Limtre, including load-bearing structures in glued laminated timber.

facts.fact: Cross laminated timber was used for the stairwells, elevator shafts and balconies.
facts.quote: Cross laminated timber were used for stairwells, elevator shafts and balconies.

facts.fact: It counts as an all-timber structure, though concrete slabs were used on the top seven floors for comfort and acoustics.
facts.quote: In Mjøstårnet, concrete slabs were used on the top seven floors in order to handle comfort criteria and acoustics.

facts.fact: The Pyramids are three pyramidal office buildings in the College Park neighbourhood of Indianapolis, Indiana.
facts.quote: The Pyramids are three 11-story, pyramidal office buildings that are part of a 200-acre (810,000 m) commercial development in the College Park neighborhood of Indianapolis, Indiana, United States.

facts.fact: They were built between 1967 and 1972 for the College Life Insurance Company to a design by Kevin Roche.
facts.quote: They were constructed between 1967 and 1972 by the College Life Insurance Company (now part of Americo Life) using a design by architect Kevin Roche.

facts.fact: Roche's plan was for nine identical office towers so that the company could build space as it needed it, but only three were built.
facts.quote: It decided on a plan by Kevin Roche consisting of nine identical office towers each eleven stories tall and each containing 120,000 square feet (11,000 m). This would permit it to build towers as it needed additional office space without leaving buildings idle or underused.

facts.fact: Each tower has two reinforced concrete walls that carry the floors and hold the service cores, with the other two walls in blue glass.
facts.quote: Each tower is made up of two walls of reinforced concrete from which project the unobstructed office floors. Those concrete walls provide support for the floors as well as serving as L-shaped service cores, containing elevators, stairwells, and mechanical systems.

facts.fact: The towers are described as abstract and sculptural, with opaque concrete facing the highway and reflective glass facing the lake.
facts.quote: The buildings have been described as "abstract" and "sculptural" based on their use of opaque concrete walls facing Interstate 465 and reflective blue glass facing the interior lake of the complex.

facts.fact: The buildings are linked to one another by underground and above-ground passages.
facts.quote: The other two walls are covered in blue exterior glass and each building is connected to the others via underground and above-ground passages.

facts.fact: They are among Roche's most notable works and contributed to his being awarded the Pritzker Prize.
facts.quote: The Pyramids are among Roche's most notable works and contributed to his being awarded the Pritzker Prize.

facts.fact: A 2021 panel of AIA Indianapolis members named them among the ten most architecturally significant buildings completed in the city since World War II.
facts.quote: In 2021, a six-person panel of American Institute of Architects (AIA) Indianapolis members identified The Pyramids among the ten most "architecturally significant" buildings completed in the city since World War II.

facts.fact: It is a multi-purpose indoor arena in the Bercy neighbourhood of the 12th arrondissement of Paris.
facts.quote: Accor Arena (originally known as the Palais Omnisports de Paris-Bercy), also known as Bercy Arena, is a multi-purpose indoor arena in Paris, France.

facts.fact: It mainly hosts sporting events and concerts.
facts.quote: it mainly hosts sporting events and concerts, and can accommodate up to 20,300 people.

facts.fact: It was designed by the architectural firm Andrault-Parat, Jean Prouvé and Aydin Guvan.
facts.quote: Designed by the architectural firm Andrault-Parat, Jean Prouvé and Aydin Guvan, the pyramidal arena's sloping walls are covered with a lawn.

facts.fact: The arena is pyramidal and its sloping walls are covered with a lawn.
facts.quote: Designed by the architectural firm Andrault-Parat, Jean Prouvé and Aydin Guvan, the pyramidal arena's sloping walls are covered with a lawn.

facts.fact: The inaugural concert was given by L'Orchestre de Paris on 17 February 1984.
facts.quote: The inaugural concert was given by L'Orchestre de Paris on 17 February 1984, when Lorin Maazel conducted the orchestra and massed choirs in a performance of Berlioz's Grande Messe des Morts.

facts.fact: It was a venue for the 2024 Summer Olympics, hosting gymnastics and the basketball medal games.
facts.quote: The arena was a venue for the 2024 Summer Olympics, hosting the artistic and trampoline gymnastics events, followed by the basketball bronze and gold medal games for both genders.

facts.fact: It is a high-rise office building in the Sendling-Westpark district of Munich, built between 2006 and 2011.
facts.quote: The ADAC Headquarters (German: ADAC-Zentrale) is a high-rise office building in the Sendling-Westpark district of Munich, Germany. Built between 2006 and 2011, the tower stands at 93 m (305 ft) tall with 23 floors and is the current 7th tallest building in Munich.

facts.fact: Sauerbruch Hutton won a restricted competition for the design, chosen on 23 March 2004.
facts.quote: In addition to first prize for the design by Sauerbruch Hutton, two third prizes went to the Munich firms Goetz and Hootz and Allmann Sattler Wappner.

facts.fact: It consists of a five-storey base shaped like an amoeba with rounded edges, with 18 high-rise floors on top.
facts.quote: Construction began in 2006 and consists of two main sections: a five- storey base, which is shaped like an amoeba and is characterised by its rounded edges, and on top of this a further 18 high-rise floors.

facts.fact: The tower's glass facade uses 1,152 elements in 22 colours that play like a mosaic.
facts.quote: The 22 different colours of the 1,152 façade elements develop their play of colours like a mosaic.

facts.fact: The colours were chosen mainly from the client's brand colour.
facts.quote: The colours were chosen primarily based on the brand colour of the client.

facts.fact: Besides offices, the complex includes a visitor and conference centre, a casino, a printing works and a television studio.
facts.quote: In addition to the individual and open-plan offices, the entire complex includes a visitor and conference centre, a casino, a printing works, meeting rooms with video conferencing equipment and a television studio.

facts.fact: The site includes the listed Sander Villa from 1909, renovated to largely restore its original facade and now used as the library, archive and conference room.
facts.quote: The historic Sander Villa on the property was renovated by the ADAC, largely restoring the original façade. It is now used by the association's library and archive, as well as a conference room.

facts.fact: Cost increases and a dispute led Sauerbruch Hutton to terminate its contract in September 2009, and a legal dispute followed.
facts.quote: The tensions that then arose between the ADAC and the general planning team ultimately led to Sauerbruch Hutton terminating the contract in September 2009.

facts.fact: It was built in 1909 in the Moabit district of Berlin and is the best-known work of architect Peter Behrens.
facts.quote: The AEG turbine factory was built in 1909, at Huttenstraße 12–16 in the Moabit district of Berlin. It is the best-known work of architect Peter Behrens.

facts.fact: It is considered the first attempt to bring restrained modern design to industrial architecture.
facts.quote: The 100 m long steel-framed building with 15 m tall glass windows on either side is considered the first attempt to introduce restrained modern design to industrial architecture.

facts.fact: Behrens worked as lead architect with the engineer Karl Bernhard.
facts.quote: The turbine hall was built in 1909 under Peter Behrens as lead architect and engineer Karl Bernhard at the corner of Huttenstraße and Berlichingenstraße streets in Berlin-Moabit.

facts.fact: Behrens had been employed by AEG since 1907 as artistic consultant, designing its products, logo and graphics.
facts.quote: More than an architect, Behrens was employed by AEG since 1907 as an artistic consultant, and designed the company's electrical products, as well as its logo and other company graphics.

facts.fact: The steel columns appear unadorned on the outside, with bolts and joints visible and large glass windows between them.
facts.quote: The steel columns appear on the outside unadorned, with bolts and joints visible, with huge glass windows between, angled slightly inwards towards the top.

facts.fact: The gable ends are reinforced concrete with metal strapping on the piers that gives a rusticated look, and the firm's logo is cast into the concrete.
facts.quote: The gable ends are constructed of reinforced concrete, with metal strapping on the piers either side creating a rusticated appearance, and the firm's logo is cast in the concrete of the gable.

facts.fact: David Watkin describes it as a "temple of power", and Tom Wilkinson likens it to an "up-to-date edition of the Parthenon".
facts.quote: David Watkin describes it as a "temple of power". Similarly, Tom Wilkinson likens it to an "up-to-date edition of the Parthenon".

facts.fact: It is still used to make turbines a hundred years later.
facts.quote: This factory was actually designed with such foresight that it still serves the same purpose of producing turbines, a hundred years later.

facts.fact: It is an independent, privately funded contemporary art museum in Lasipalatsi on Mannerheimintie boulevard in Helsinki, named after the publisher and arts patron Amos Anderson.
facts.quote: Amos Rex is an independent, privately funded contemporary art museum named after the publisher and arts patron Amos Anderson and located in Lasipalatsi, on Mannerheimintie boulevard in Helsinki, Finland.

facts.fact: The museum was built beneath Lasipalatsi Square and opened to the public in August 2018.
facts.quote: The construction of the new museum started in January 2016 and it opened to the public in August 2018.

facts.fact: JKMM Architects conceptualised the design.
facts.quote: The design of the new Amos Rex was conceptualised by JKMM Architects, whose other works include the Turku Main Library and the Finnish pavilion at the 2010 Shanghai World Expo.

facts.fact: The aim was to blend modernity and heritage, putting the museum underground while respecting the historic Lasipalatsi building.
facts.quote: The goal was to create a space that blends modernity and heritage, with the new museum integrated beneath Lasipalatsi Square while respecting the historical significance of the Lasipalatsi building.

facts.fact: Its rooftop domes act as both art elements and skylights that let natural light into the underground spaces.
facts.quote: A key feature of the museum’s design is its interactive rooftop domes, which serve as both artistic elements and functional skylights, allowing natural light to filter into the underground spaces.

facts.fact: Asmo Jaaksi, chief architect, said it was important to create some contact between ground level and the underground world.
facts.quote: Asmo Jaaksi, chief architect of the museum, said that it was important that some kind of contact between the ground level and the subterranean world was created.

facts.fact: The New York Times described it as topped by five conical domes that bubble up from the square like inverted craters.
facts.quote: As The New York Times writes, the museum “appears to physically resist its placement in a vast underground space, [as] it is topped by five conical domes that bubble up from the surface of the Lasipalatsi Square in downtown Helsinki like inverted craters of an alien moonscape.”

facts.fact: Inside, the exhibition room is defined by ceiling discs that conceal technical elements while also serving aesthetic and acoustic functions.
facts.quote: Inside, the exhibition room is defined by its distinctive ceiling discs, which conceal technical elements while also serving aesthetic and acoustic functions.

facts.fact: It is a grade II listed residential and shopping centre in Bloomsbury, London, between Brunswick Square and Russell Square.
facts.quote: The Brunswick Centre is a grade II listed residential and shopping centre in Bloomsbury, London, England. It is located between Brunswick Square and Russell Square and is administratively in the London Borough of Camden.

facts.fact: It replaced streets of run-down Georgian terrace housing.
facts.quote: The centre replaced streets of run-down Georgian era terrace housing.

facts.fact: Patrick Hodgkinson designed it in the mid-1960s, based on studies by Leslie Martin.
facts.quote: It was designed by Patrick Hodgkinson in the mid-1960s, based on studies by Leslie Martin.

facts.fact: It was initially planned as a private development at a time when private mixed-use development in the UK was rare.
facts.quote: It was initially planned as a private development at a time when private, mixed-use development in the UK was rare.

facts.fact: Building started in 1967 and was completed in 1972, though it fell short of its intended size because the Ministry of Defence would not release a leased site.
facts.quote: Building started in 1967 and was completed in 1972, though the building fell some way short of its intended size.

facts.fact: Hodgkinson intended the blocks to be painted cream, a Georgian shade, as a homage to the terraces that stood there before.
facts.quote: In Hodgkinson's design, the blocks would have been painted cream, a shade typical of the Georgian period, as a homage to the terraced houses that previously stood on the site and those that still surround it.

facts.fact: The residential part was leased to Camden as council housing while the developer kept the structure and shopping areas.
facts.quote: After failing to attract sufficient private buyers on time, the residential section was leased to the London Borough of Camden for use as council housing, while the developer retained ownership of the structure and shopping areas.

facts.fact: It was listed Grade II in 2000 despite being widely disliked by those unsympathetic to modernist architecture.
facts.quote: Despite being widely disliked by those who are unsympathetic to modernist architecture, it was listed Grade II on the National Heritage List for England in 2000.

facts.fact: A renovation that began in November 2002 included painting the blocks in their originally planned colour and commissioning Susanna Heron to add water features to the central space.
facts.quote: Plans for renovation had repeatedly been blocked by residents' committees but in November 2002, the £22 million project began.  This included the painting of the blocks in their originally-planned colour and the commissioning of artist Susanna Heron to introduce water features to the central space.

facts.fact: It is a communications and observation tower in downtown Toronto, completed in 1976.
facts.quote: The CN Tower (French: Tour CN) is a 553.3-metre-high (1,815.3 ft) communications and observation tower in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Completed in 1976, it is located in downtown Toronto, built on the former Railway Lands.

facts.fact: Its name refers to Canadian National, the railway company that built it.
facts.quote: Its name "CN" refers to Canadian National, the railway company that built the tower.

facts.fact: It was conceived in 1968 as a large television and radio communication platform for the Toronto area, to show the strength of Canadian industry.
facts.quote: The original concept of the CN Tower was first conceived in 1968 when the Canadian National Railway wanted to build a large television and radio communication platform to serve the Toronto area, and to demonstrate the strength of Canadian industry and CN in particular.

facts.fact: New reflective skyscrapers reduced the quality of broadcast signals, creating a need for higher antennas.
facts.quote: The reflective nature of the new buildings reduced the quality of broadcast signals, indicating a need for new, higher antennas that were at least 300 m (980 ft) tall.

facts.fact: The first plan was a tripod of three cylindrical pillars, which evolved into a single hexagonal core with three support legs forming a Y-shape at ground level.
facts.quote: As the design effort continued, it evolved into the current design with a single continuous hexagonal core to The Top, with three support legs blended into the hexagon below the main level, forming a large Y-shape structure at the ground level.

facts.fact: The main pillar was built with a hydraulically raised slipform, a platform that raised itself on jacks as the concrete below set.
facts.quote: To create the main support pillar, workers constructed a hydraulically raised slipform at the base. This was a fairly unprecedented engineering feat on its own, consisting of a large metal platform that raised itself on jacks at about 6 m (20 ft) per day as the concrete below set.

facts.fact: The six elevators sit in the three inverted angles of the hexagonal shape, and their shafts are lined with glass.
facts.quote: The tower's six elevators are located in the three inverted angles created by the Tower's hexagonal shape (two elevators per angle). Each of the three elevator shafts is lined with glass, allowing for views of the city as the glass-windowed elevators make their way through the tower.

facts.fact: It held the record for the world's tallest free-standing structure for 32 years, until the Burj Khalifa surpassed it in 2007.
facts.quote: The CN Tower held the record for the world's tallest free-standing structure for 32 years, from 1975 until 2007, when it was surpassed by the Burj Khalifa, and was the world's tallest tower until 2009 when it was surpassed by the Canton Tower.

facts.fact: In 1995 the American Society of Civil Engineers declared it one of the modern Seven Wonders of the World.
facts.quote: In 1995, the CN Tower was declared one of the modern Seven Wonders of the World by the American Society of Civil Engineers.

facts.fact: It is a brutalist office building used by Petrobras in the Centro neighbourhood of Rio de Janeiro, nicknamed Edise by its employees.
facts.quote: The Petrobras Headquarters building, nicknamed Edise by the employees working in it, is a brutalist office building used by Petrobras in the Centro neighbourhood of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

facts.fact: The architect was Roberto Luís Gandolfi.
facts.quote: The building's architect was Roberto Luís Gandolfi.

facts.fact: Gandolfi's design was chosen through a national competition organised by the Brazilian Institute of Architects.
facts.quote: Through a national competition organized by the Brazilian Institute of Architects, Roberto Luis Gandolfi's design was chosen from more than 200 entries from construction firms to house Petrobras.

facts.fact: The facade spaces create interaction between indoors and outdoors and give protection from the sun and heat.
facts.quote: the façade spaces create interaction between the indoor and outdoor areas, providing protection from the sun and heat.

facts.fact: It is located on Avenida República do Chile, next to the Metropolitan Cathedral.
facts.quote: Considered a landmark in national architecture, the building is located on Avenida República do Chile, next to the Metropolitan Cathedral.

facts.fact: It has been revitalised for the first time in nearly 50 years with sustainability and inclusiveness measures.
facts.quote: In 2021, Edise was revitalized for the first time in nearly 50 years, with the implementation of sustainability and inclusiveness measures.

facts.fact: The gardens designed by Roberto Burle Marx are to be revitalised, keeping their original layout, which is listed by the city.
facts.quote: The gardens, both indoors and outdoors, designed by Roberto Burle Marx, will also be revitalized, maintaining their original layout, which is listed by the city.

facts.fact: It is a Category A listed student hall of residence of the University of St Andrews in Fife, Scotland.
facts.quote: Andrew Melville Hall is a Category A listed student hall of residence of the University of St Andrews located in St Andrews, Fife, Scotland.

facts.fact: James Stirling designed it in the New Brutalist style.
facts.quote: Designed in the New Brutalist style by the renowned architect James Stirling, Andrew Melville Hall was built during a major expansion of the University in the 1960s using prefabricated concrete modules.

facts.fact: It was built during a major expansion of the university in the 1960s using prefabricated concrete modules.
facts.quote: Designed in the New Brutalist style by the renowned architect James Stirling, Andrew Melville Hall was built during a major expansion of the University in the 1960s using prefabricated concrete modules.

facts.fact: Errors in construction meant extensive remedial work was needed over several decades, and plans for further buildings to the same design were abandoned.
facts.quote: Errors in construction meant that extensive remedial work was required over several decades. Plans for further buildings to the same design were abandoned.

facts.fact: It stands prominently on the North Haugh on a ridge overlooking the St Andrews Links.
facts.quote: It is of a striking design and is situated prominently at the North Haugh on a ridge overlooking the St Andrews Links.

facts.fact: The hall is said to resemble passing ships, a common theme of the architect's style.
facts.quote: The hall resembles passing ships, a common theme of the architect's style.

facts.fact: The building's geometry is reflected in the irregular octagonal shape of the bedrooms.
facts.quote: The building's striking geometry is reflected in the irregular octagonal shape of the bedrooms.

facts.fact: Glass enclosures shaped like greenhouses on top of some blocks give natural light to the stairwells.
facts.quote: Blocks A, D and E have glass enclosures similar in shape to a garden greenhouse atop them to provide natural light to their stairwells; this has led to the top floor of these blocks being called "the greenhouse".

facts.fact: It was included in DoCoMoMo's 1993 list of Key Scottish Monuments and listed Category A in 2011.
facts.quote: It was included in DoCoMoMo's 1993 list of Key Scottish Monuments and was ranked number 12 in the top 100 Scottish buildings of the last 50 years.  The building was listed Category A in 2011.

facts.fact: It is a skyscraper on the Wilhelminapier in Rotterdam, designed by the Office for Metropolitan Architecture.
facts.quote: De Rotterdam is a skyscraper on the Wilhelminapier in Rotterdam, designed by the Office for Metropolitan Architecture in 1998 and developed by Edge.

facts.fact: The design provides space for offices, a hotel and apartments.
facts.quote: The design provides space for offices, a hotel and apartments.

facts.fact: It consists of three interconnected towers that share a base which includes six floors.
facts.quote: The building consists of three interconnected towers that share a thirty feet high base which includes six floors.

facts.fact: The lower two layers form a large glass plinth.
facts.quote: The lower two layers form a large glass plinth.

facts.fact: At about 90 metres above ground the towers are shifted a few metres in different directions, which enhances wind stability and provides space for terraces.
facts.quote: At about 90 meters above ground the towers – known as West Tower, Mid Tower and East Tower– are shifted a few meters in different directions, which enhances the wind stability and provides space for terraces.

facts.fact: In the original design the towers did not touch, but they are now connected in a few places to simplify the play of forces and keep construction affordable.
facts.quote: In the original design the towers did not touch each other, but in order to simplify the play of forces and to keep the construction affordable they are now connected in a few places.

facts.fact: The facade offers the option of natural ventilation.
facts.quote: The facade provides the option of natural ventilation.

facts.fact: OMA defines the grouping of functions in blocks that meet at various places as a vertical city.
facts.quote: The functions are grouped into blocks, but the different user groups meet at various places in the building, a concept that is defined by the Office for Metropolitan Architecture as a vertical city.

facts.fact: It was the broadcast headquarters, studios and master control for all French-language radio and television services of the CBC, in Montreal.
facts.quote: Maison de Radio-Canada (French pronunciation: [mɛzɔ̃ də ʁadjo kanada]; English: CBC House), located in Montreal, Quebec, Canada, was the broadcast headquarters, studios and master control for all French-language radio and television services of the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (known in French as Société Radio-Canada/SRC) including its flagship station CBFT-DT.

facts.fact: To build it, most of the working-class Faubourg à m'lasse neighbourhood had to be demolished.
facts.quote: For the building itself to be built, most of the Faubourg à m'lasse working-class neighbourhood had to be demolished.

facts.fact: The last house was evacuated on October 1, 1963, so demolition could clear the land.
facts.quote: On October 1, 1963, the last house was evacuated so the demolition project could go ahead to clear land for the facility.

facts.fact: The old building's address is 1400 René Lévesque Boulevard East, named for the former premier who was once a CBC reporter and commentator.
facts.quote: The street address of the old Maison de Radio-Canada is 1400 René Lévesque Boulevard East, named for former premier René Lévesque who was once a reporter and commentator for the CBC.

facts.fact: Redevelopment plans for the site would relink the street grid that was cut by the 1960s razing of the neighbourhood.
facts.quote: Furthermore, the new development would relink the street grid through the site, following the 1960s razing of a working-class neighbourhood popularly known as Faubourg à m'lasse to make way for the Radio-Canada complex.

facts.fact: A new building at 1000 Papineau Avenue was inaugurated on September 7, 2022.
facts.quote: The new building, inaugurated in September 7, 2022, is located at 1000 Papineau Avenue.

facts.fact: As of April 2025, most buildings of the old complex had been demolished to make way for a future residential project.
facts.quote: As of April 2025, most buildings of the old Maison de Radio-Canada were demolished to take place for a future residential project.

facts.fact: It is a 21-story residential building at 200 East 66th Street on the Upper East Side of Manhattan, constructed between 1949 and 1951.
facts.quote: Manhattan House is a 21-story residential condominium building at 200 East 66th Street on the Upper East Side of Manhattan in New York City, New York, United States. The building was designed in the modern style by Gordon Bunshaft of Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM), in partnership with the firm of Albert Mayer and Julian Whittlesey. It occupies a full city block bounded by Third Avenue to the west, 66th Street to the north, Second Avenue to the east, and 65th Street to the south. Constructed between 1949 and 1951, Manhattan House was developed by the New York Life Insurance Company as a middle-class apartment building.

facts.fact: Gordon Bunshaft of SOM designed it with Mayer & Whittlesey.
facts.quote: Manhattan House was designed in the modernist style by Gordon Bunshaft of architectural firm Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM), in partnership with the firm Mayer & Whittlesey, composed of Albert Mayer and Julian Whittlesey.

facts.fact: New York Life developed it as a middle-class apartment building.
facts.quote: Constructed between 1949 and 1951, Manhattan House was developed by the New York Life Insurance Company as a middle-class apartment building.

facts.fact: The building has a central spine with five wings facing north and south, and it is set back from both side streets.
facts.quote: Manhattan House consists of a central "spine" with five wings each facing north and south, as well as low-rise retail podiums to the west and east. The structure is set back from both 65th and 66th Streets and only occupies about two-fifths of the lot.

facts.fact: To allow a tall building with fewer setbacks, New York Life donated the northern part of the site to the city and placed a garden on the southern part.
facts.quote: To allow the construction of a tall structure with fewer setbacks, New York Life donated the northern part of the site to the New York City government, and it placed a garden on the southern part.

facts.fact: It was one of the first buildings in New York to use pale white brick as its main facade material.
facts.quote: Manhattan House was one of the first in New York City to use pale white brick as the primary material in its facade.

facts.fact: The brick was glazed so that dirt would wash off in the rain.
facts.quote: The brick was glazed, which allowed dirt to wash off in the rain.

facts.fact: Above the fifth floor, apartments with at least three rooms have private balconies next to the living or dining rooms.
facts.quote: Above the fifth floor, apartments with at least three rooms contain private balconies, which adjoin the living or dining rooms of each unit.

facts.fact: Older apartment buildings in New York put their facades on the lot line and gardens inside; Manhattan House set the building back with gardens outside.
facts.quote: This contrasted with older apartment buildings in New York City, where the exterior facades extended to the lot line and the gardens were placed within the building's interior.

facts.fact: It was designated a New York City landmark on October 30, 2007.
facts.quote: The LPC designated Manhattan House as a New York City landmark on October 30, 2007, and sales of condominiums began the next month.

facts.fact: Robert A. M. Stern considered it the most literal manifestation in New York of Le Corbusier's postwar conception of vertical living.
facts.quote: Stern considered the building to be "the most literal manifestation in New York of Le Corbusier's postwar conception of vertical living", and the LPC similarly compared Manhattan House to Le Corbusier's principle of unité d'habitation.

facts.fact: Its design inspired numerous other white-brick buildings around New York City.
facts.quote: Its design did inspire that of numerous other white-brick structures around New York City, including 2 Fifth Avenue, Washington Square Village, Stewart House, Imperial House, and the buildings at 215 East 68th Street and 500 East 77th Street.

facts.fact: It is one of the most studied of the nine built houses designed by Louis Kahn, in Philadelphia.
facts.quote: The Margaret Esherick House in Philadelphia is one of the most studied of the nine built houses designed by American architect Louis Kahn.

facts.fact: Chestnut Hill bookstore owner Margaret Esherick commissioned it, and it was completed in 1961.
facts.quote: Commissioned by Chestnut Hill bookstore owner Margaret Esherick, the house was completed in 1961.

facts.fact: The house is noted for its spatial organisation and for the ventilation and natural light from its unusual window and shutter configuration.
facts.quote: The house is noted especially for its spatial organization and for the ventilation and natural lighting provided by its unusual window and shutter configuration.

facts.fact: It is a flat-roofed, rectangular solid with its long side facing the street, built mainly of concrete block with stucco facing.
facts.quote: The 2500 sq feet (230 sq m), single-bedroom house is a flat-roofed, rectangular solid with its long side facing the street. The primary building material is concrete block with stucco facing.

facts.fact: Kahn divided buildings into served spaces and servant spaces, and here they alternate as four parallel two-story strips running front to back.
facts.quote: Kahn often divided his buildings into what he called served spaces (primary areas) and servant spaces (corridors, bathrooms, etc.)   The Esherick house is organized into four alternating served and servant spaces, which in this case are parallel two-story strips that run the full width of the house between front to back.

facts.fact: The two-story living room has a built-in bookcase across most of its front wall, since Margaret Esherick was a bookseller.
facts.quote: Most of its front wall is occupied by a built-in bookcase (Margaret Esherick was a bookseller) that reaches up to the horizontal window at the second story.

facts.fact: The kitchen of wood and copper was made by the craftsman and artist Wharton Esherick, Margaret's uncle.
facts.quote: Its copper and wood kitchen was created by Wharton Esherick, a nationally known craftsman and artist who was also her uncle.

facts.fact: Each side of the house has a different window and ventilation configuration.
facts.quote: Each side of the house has a window and ventilation configuration that is distinctly different from that of the other three sides.

facts.fact: At the rear, large fixed single-pane windows are flanked by stacks of shutters that can be opened in any combination, linking indoors and outdoors.
facts.quote: On both sides of each pair of these large windows are two-story stacks of shutters, four shutters per stack.  They also reach from the bottom of the house to the top, and they can be opened and closed in any combination, creating an elaborate set of possible connections between indoors and outdoors.

facts.fact: It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2023.
facts.quote: In 2023, the house was listed on the National Register of Historic Places by the United States Department of the Interior.

facts.fact: Built in the mid-1960s, it was the third home of the Whitney Museum of American Art.
facts.quote: Built from 1964 to 1966 as the third home of the Whitney Museum of American Art, it subsequently held a branch of the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Frick Collection before becoming the headquarters of Sotheby's auction house.

facts.fact: Marcel Breuer and Hamilton P. Smith were the primary architects, with Paul Weidlinger as structural engineer.
facts.quote: Marcel Breuer and Hamilton P. Smith were the primary architects, with Michael H. Irving as the consulting architect and Paul Weidlinger as the structural engineer.

facts.fact: It was Breuer's first museum commission and his only remaining work in Manhattan.
facts.quote: It was also his first museum commission, and his first and only remaining work in Manhattan.

facts.fact: It has exterior faces of variegated granite and exposed concrete and uses stark angular shapes.
facts.quote: The structure has exterior faces of variegated granite and exposed concrete and makes use of stark angular shapes, including cantilevered floors progressively extending atop its entryway, resembling an inverted ziggurat.

facts.fact: Its upper galleries cantilever outward over the Madison Avenue entrance, forming a portico lit at night.
facts.quote: The cantilevered facade functions as a portico, and the spaces underneath are illuminated at night.

facts.fact: Breuer chose coarse granite, split slate floors, bronze doors and fittings, and teakwood, materials meant to weather and age well.
facts.quote: The building utilizes "close-to-earth" materials that weather over time, intended to express age beautifully. Breuer chose coarse granite, split slate floors, bronze doors and fittings, and teakwood.

facts.fact: Sources describe its style as Brutalist or as part of the wider Modernist movement.
facts.quote: Sources variously describe the building's architectural style to be Brutalist or part of the larger Modernist movement.

facts.fact: Its design influenced later projects, including the Cleveland Museum of Art's north wing and Atlanta's Central Library.
facts.quote: The building defined the Whitney Museum's image for nearly 50 years, influencing subsequent projects such as the Cleveland Museum of Art's north wing and Atlanta's Central Library.

facts.fact: It is the main chapel of the Ibaraki Kasugaoka Church, built in 1989 in Ibaraki, Osaka Prefecture.
facts.quote: It was built in 1989, in the city of Ibaraki, Osaka Prefecture.

facts.fact: It is one of Tadao Ando's most famous designs.
facts.quote: This building is one of the most famous designs of Japanese architect Tadao Ando.

facts.fact: The church was planned as an add-on to a wooden chapel and minister's house already on the site.
facts.quote: The church was planned as an add-on to the wooden chapel and minister's house that already existed at the site.

facts.fact: A wall angled at 15 degrees cuts through the concrete volume, dividing the chapel from the entrance area.
facts.quote: The Church of the Light consists of three 5.9m concrete cubes (5.9 m wide × 17.7 m long × 5.9 m high) penetrated by a wall angled at 15°, dividing the cube into the chapel and the entrance area.

facts.fact: The benches and floor boards are made of re-purposed scaffolding used in the construction.
facts.quote: The benches, along with the floor boards, are made of re-purposed scaffolding used in the construction.

facts.fact: A cruciform is cut into the concrete behind the altar, and it is lit during the day.
facts.quote: A cruciform is cut into the concrete behind the altar, and lit during the day.

facts.fact: Light enters through a cross cut in the wall behind the altar, aligned with the joints in the concrete.
facts.quote: In the chapel light enters from behind the altar from a cross cut in the concrete wall that extends vertically from floor to ceiling and horizontally from wall to wall, aligning perfectly with the joints in the concrete.

facts.fact: Ando drew on Zen philosophies, and one theme here is the dual nature of existence.
facts.quote: Tadao Ando often uses Zen philosophies when conceptualizing his structures. One theme he expresses in this work is the dual nature of existence.

facts.fact: It is a skyscraper in central São Paulo, designed by Oscar Niemeyer with structural design by engineer Joaquim Cardozo.
facts.quote: It is one of the symbols of modern Brazilian architecture, designed by architect Oscar Niemeyer with structural design by engineer Joaquim Cardozo, aiming to celebrate the Fourth Centenary of the city of São Paulo.

facts.fact: It was inaugurated in 1966.
facts.quote: The Edifício Copan (Copan Building), or just Copan, is one of the most important and emblematic buildings in the city of São Paulo, located at number 200 Avenida Ipiranga, in the city center, and was inaugurated in 1966.

facts.fact: Niemeyer was personally responsible for its sinuous facade.
facts.quote: Niemeyer was personally responsible for the building's famous sinuous façade.
