facts.fact: The idea was a building open to a mixed cross-section of Brazilian society.
facts.quote: The idea was a building open to a mixed cross-section of Brazilian society.

facts.fact: The original project envisioned two buildings, the other a hotel, but only the residential building was built.
facts.quote: The original project envisioned two buildings, the other being a hotel, but in the end only the residential building was built.

facts.fact: The name is an acronym for its original developer, Companhia Pan-Americana de Hotéis e Turismo.
facts.quote: The building's name is an acronym for its original developer, Companhia Pan-Americana de Hotéis e Turismo (Portuguese for "Pan-American Hotels and Tourism Company").

facts.fact: It has the largest reinforced concrete structure in Brazil.
facts.quote: The building has the largest reinforced concrete structure in the country, 115 meters high (377 ft.), 32 floors and 120 thousand square meters of built area, divided into six blocks, with a total of 1,160 apartments of varying sizes, according to an estimate of five thousand residents from different social classes and more than seventy commercial establishments.

facts.fact: Since 2014 a transparent drape has covered the building to protect pedestrians from loose facade tiles.
facts.quote: Since 2014 the entire building has been covered by a transparent blue-black drape, to protect pedestrians from the facade's loose mosaic tiles.

facts.fact: It is one of ten library parks in Medellín, Colombia, in the Belén commune.
facts.quote: Bethlehem Library (Spanish: Parque Biblioteca Belén) is one of ten library parks in Medellín, Colombia, located in Comuna 16.

facts.fact: It was designed by Japanese architect Hiroshi Naito in collaboration with the University of Tokyo.
facts.quote: The library was designed by Japanese architect Hiroshi Naito in collaboration with the University of Tokyo.

facts.fact: The park has public spaces with three ambiances: a green plaza, a water plaza and a plaza for the public.
facts.quote: The library park has public spaces with three different ambiances: a green plaza, a water plaza, and a plaza for the public.

facts.fact: The design was donated by a group of University of Tokyo architects under Naito, as part of an exchange begun in 2006.
facts.quote: Universities in Colombia began a program of sharing with the University of Tokyo in 2006. As part of this exchange, a group of architects from the University of Tokyo, under the direction of Hiroshi Naito, donated the design of Bethlehem Library.

facts.fact: It is a town house in Brussels designed by Victor Horta for Edmond van Eetvelde, in Art Nouveau style.
facts.quote: It was designed by Victor Horta for Edmond van Eetvelde, administrator of Congo Free State, and built between 1895 and 1898, in Art Nouveau style.

facts.fact: Horta added two extensions, between 1898 and 1901.
facts.quote: Two extensions, also designed by Horta, were added between 1898 and 1901.

facts.fact: It is part of a UNESCO World Heritage listing of four Horta town houses, added in 2000.
facts.quote: Together with three other town houses of Victor Horta, including Horta's own house and workshop, it was added to the UNESCO World Heritage list in 2000 as the core of epoch-making urban residences that Horta designed before 1900.

facts.fact: Steel and glass were visibly used, which was new for prestigious private houses at the time.
facts.quote: The visible application of "industrial" materials, such as steel and glass, was a novel for prestigious private dwellings at the time.

facts.fact: Horta also used a hanging steel construction for the facade.
facts.quote: In the Hôtel van Eetvelde, Victor Horta also used a hanging steel construction for the façade.

facts.fact: The interior gets extra light through a central reception room covered by a stained glass cupola.
facts.quote: The interior receives additional lighting through a central reception room covered by a stained glass cupola.

facts.fact: The interior revolves around an octagonal rotunda under a skylight.
facts.quote: The interior of the central building revolves around an octagonal rotunda surmounted by a skylight.

facts.fact: The rotunda works as a small winter garden surrounded by a circulation area linking the living room, dining room and stairwell.
facts.quote: Horta combined here a rest area and a movement area; the rotunda has the function of a small living room or Winter Garden, but it is surrounded by a circulation area that provides the connection with the living room, the dining room and stairwell.

facts.fact: It is the Paris headquarters of Radio France, nicknamed the "maison ronde".
facts.quote: Maison de la Radio et de la Musique (French pronunciation: [mɛzɔ̃ də la ʁadjo e də la myzik]), nicknamed “maison ronde” (“the round house”) is the headquarters of Radio France.

facts.fact: It is built as a huge ring with a central utility tower and houses offices, broadcasting studios and performance spaces.
facts.quote: Built in the shape of a huge ring 500 meters in circumference, with a central utility tower, the building houses the administrative offices, broadcasting studios, and performance spaces for all of Radio France's national stations and its four permanent ensembles—Orchestre philharmonique de Radio France, Orchestre national de France, Chœur de Radio France and Maîtrise de Radio France.

facts.fact: Henry Bernard designed it and it was completed in 1963.
facts.quote: The building was designed by Henry Bernard and completed in 1963.

facts.fact: The government chose a site near the Eiffel Tower and its radio transmitters, on the Seine in the 16th arrondissement.
facts.quote: Previously the site of a gasworks which had been decommissioned in 1928, and then a stadium, the location was considered ideal because of its proximity to the Eiffel Tower and its radio transmitters.

facts.fact: Henry Bernard won the 1953 competition from 26 entrants.
facts.quote: The winner from the 26 entrants was Henry Bernard who had won the Prix de Rome in architecture in 1938 and had participated in the post-war reconstruction of Caen.

facts.fact: A major renovation by Architecture-Studio, with acoustical engineering by Nagata Acoustics, was awarded in 2005.
facts.quote: In October 2005 the contract was awarded to Architecture-Studio, with acoustical engineering by Nagata Acoustics and Lamoureux and scenography works by Changement à vue, and work began shortly thereafter.

facts.fact: The Grand Auditorium, created from the old Studios 102 and 103, has walls and balcony facades covered in faceted panels of birch, beech and cherry wood.
facts.quote: The walls and balcony facades are covered in faceted panels of birch, beech and cherry wood.

facts.fact: Studio 104 has been known since 1963 for its superior acoustics.
facts.quote: It seats 852 people and has been known since the Maison's construction in 1963 for its superior acoustics.

facts.fact: Godard's film Alphaville was partly shot there, using recently built modernist glass and concrete buildings that were still considered new and strange.
facts.quote: Instead, the film used recently built modernist glass and concrete buildings such as the Maison and the CNIT that in 1965 were still considered new and strange architectural designs.

facts.fact: It is a museum in Fjærland, Vestland county, Norway.
facts.quote: The Norwegian Glacier Museum (Norwegian: Norsk Bremuseum) is a museum in Fjærland, Vestland county, Norway.

facts.fact: The building was designed by architect Sverre Fehn.
facts.quote: The building was designed by architect Sverre Fehn.

facts.fact: A later extension, also designed by Fehn, was decided in 2002.
facts.quote: In 2002 a decision was made to build an extension to the museum, which was also designed by Fehn.

facts.fact: The museum also houses the Ulltveit-Moe Climate Centre, a Fehn-designed addition that opened in 2007.
facts.quote: The museum also houses the Ulltveit-Moe Climate Centre, a Fehn-designed addition that opened in 2007.

facts.fact: Its stated purpose is to collect, create and disseminate knowledge about glaciers and climate.
facts.quote: The museum's stated purpose is to "collect, create and disseminate knowledge about glaciers and climate".

facts.fact: It provides information about the Jostedalsbreen glacier and Jostedalsbreen National Park.
facts.quote: It provides information about the glacier Jostedalsbreen and the Jostedalsbreen National Park.
